name: Yoga pose
pattern: Static postures held for a few breaths, or linked with the breath into a flow such as the sun salutation.
setup: Use a non-slip mat on a flat floor, barefoot.
Start in the base position of the pose: standing, kneeling, seated, on hands and knees, or lying down.
Set your feet and hands first, then build the pose from the ground up.

steps.text: Move into the pose slowly, stop at a firm but easy stretch, and breathe steadily for 3-5 breaths.

cues.cue: Breathe slowly through your nose; if you cannot, back off.
cues.why: Forceful breathing and pushing past your limit are among the techniques most linked to yoga injuries.
Most yoga injuries are trunk sprains and strains; deep folds and backbends load the spine most.

cues.cue: In lunges and warriors, front knee over the ankle, pointing at your toes.
cues.why: Standing poses load the knee in the side-to-side plane; letting the knee drift in adds that load.

cues.cue: Press through the whole foot: big toe, little toe, heel.
cues.why: Every standing pose works the ankle; a stable foot base controls balance.

cues.cue: Bend your knees in folds and down dog if your back rounds.
cues.why: Soft knees let the hips tip forward so the stretch moves out of the lower back.

breathing: Slow nasal breaths. In many flows you breathe in as you open or lift, and out as you fold or twist.

tempo.note: Hold most poses for 3-5 slow breaths (about 20-40 s). In a flow, one movement per breath.

mistakes.name: Front knee falls in
mistakes.looks: In a lunge or warrior the front knee drifts inside the big toe.
mistakes.fix: Push the knee out over your little toes, keep the front heel down.
mistakes.why: It raises the side-to-side load on the knee.

mistakes.name: Low back dumps in backbends
mistakes.looks: In cobra or upward dog the bend is all in the lower back and the shoulders hunch up.
mistakes.fix: Lift through the chest, shoulders down and back, legs active.
mistakes.why: The lower back takes the bend that the upper back and hips should share.

mistakes.name: Back rounds in folds
mistakes.looks: In forward folds and down dog the back curves like a C and the hips stay tucked.
mistakes.fix: Bend your knees and tip from the hips, chest toward the thighs.
mistakes.why: Rounding moves the stretch from the hamstrings to the spine.

mistakes.name: Weight on the neck in inversions
mistakes.looks: In shoulder stand, plow or headstand the neck is crushed and the body sinks.
mistakes.fix: Weight on the shoulders and forearms, never turn your head; use a folded blanket or skip it.
mistakes.why: Headstand and shoulder stand are the poses most often reported in yoga injury cases.

safety: Beginners: skip headstand, full lotus and forceful breathing until taught in person.
Glaucoma, high blood pressure or eye surgery: avoid inversions (head below the heart for long).
Weak bones (osteoporosis): avoid deep forward folds and loaded twists.
Adults over 65 have the highest injury rate: use a wall or chair for balance poses.
Pregnancy: avoid lying on your belly and deep twists; ask your midwife.

variants.change: Prop shortens the reach; same shape with less range.
Same pose, different camera angle or hand position.

subtypes.name: Sun salutation
subtypes.change: A flow of 12 poses, one per breath: prayer, arms up, fold, lunge, down dog, eight-limb, cobra, down dog, lunge, fold, arms up, prayer.

subtypes.name: Twists
subtypes.change: Rotate the chest about 45° over a stable pelvis; lengthen on the in-breath, turn on the out-breath. trunkRot is rotation toward the right.

subtypes.name: Arm balances (crane, peacock)
subtypes.change: Weight on bent arms, knees on the backs of the upper arms, hips high.

subtypes.name: Shoulder stand, plow, headstand
subtypes.change: Legs over the body. Shoulder stand: trunk vertical upside down (trunk 180), hands support the back. Plow: hips bend so the toes reach the floor behind your head (hipFlex about 150). Headstand: forearms and crown down, neck neutral.

subtypes.name: Pigeon and hip openers
subtypes.change: Front shin across the mat, front hip turned out; back leg long behind. Cow face: knees stacked, hands clasp behind the back.

subtypes.name: Cat and cow
subtypes.match: cat pose|cat cow|bitilasana|cow yoga pose bitilasana|tiger
subtypes.change: On hands and knees; round (cat) on the out-breath, arch (cow) on the in-breath. Tiger adds one leg reaching back.

subtypes.name: Child's pose
subtypes.change: Sit back on your heels, chest toward the thighs, arms long in front. Puppy keeps the hips over the knees.

subtypes.name: Downward-facing dog
subtypes.change: Inverted V: hips high, arms in line with the trunk, heels toward the floor. Dolphin: forearms down. Three-leg: one leg lifts in line with the trunk.

subtypes.name: Cobra, sphinx, upward dog
subtypes.change: Lying face down, chest lifts on the hands; elbows stay bent in cobra, forearms down in sphinx, arms straight and thighs off the floor in upward dog.

subtypes.name: Locust and bow
subtypes.change: Face down; chest and legs lift together (locust), or hands hold the ankles and kick into them (bow, kneeFlex about 110). Crocodile rests flat with the forehead on the hands.

subtypes.name: Camel
subtypes.change: Kneeling, hips over the knees, chest lifts and the hands reach for the heels.

subtypes.name: Bridge and wheel
subtypes.change: Lying face up, feet flat; hips lift (bridge). Wheel: hands by the ears press the whole body up into an arch.

subtypes.name: Fish
subtypes.change: Lying face up on the forearms, chest lifted, crown of the head lightly on the floor.

subtypes.name: Warrior III, half moon
subtypes.change: Standing on the left leg, trunk and right leg level like a T. Half moon opens the hips and chest to the side.

subtypes.name: Tree and standing balances
subtypes.change: Stand on the left leg; right sole on the inner thigh or calf (never on the knee), knee out. Eagle wraps the legs and arms; dancer holds the back foot.

subtypes.name: Chair
subtypes.change: Feet together, sit back as if into a chair, arms up beside the ears.

subtypes.name: Warrior II, side angle
subtypes.match: warrior ii|warrior pose ii|virabhadrasana v\. 2|reverse warrior|side angle|parsvakonasana|straight angle
subtypes.change: Wide stance, front foot forward, back foot turned in; front knee bent over the ankle, hips and chest open to the side, arms out level. Side angle leans the trunk over the front thigh.

subtypes.name: Warrior I, lunges
subtypes.change: Long stance, hips square to the front; front knee over the ankle, back leg long, arms overhead. Low lunge puts the back knee down.

subtypes.name: Triangle, pyramid
subtypes.change: Legs straight and wide; the trunk tips to the side over the front leg (shown as trunk lean), arms in one vertical line. Pyramid folds forward over the front leg instead.

subtypes.name: Standing forward fold
subtypes.match: forward bend|uttanasana|hands to feet|hastasana|wide legged|prasarita|half bend|standing seal
subtypes.change: Fold from the hips, knees soft, head hangs. Half bend: flat back halfway up, hands on the shins.

subtypes.name: Garland squat
subtypes.change: Deep squat, heels down, knees wide, elbows press the knees out with the palms together.

subtypes.name: Boat
subtypes.change: Balance on the sit bones, trunk and legs make a V, arms forward. Half boat bends the knees.

subtypes.name: Plank and chaturanga
subtypes.change: Body in one line; chaturanga lowers until the elbows are bent about 90°, elbows by the ribs.

subtypes.name: Seated forward fold
subtypes.match: spread leg forward fold|upavista|seated wide angle|head to knee|janu
subtypes.change: Seated, legs long (or wide), fold from the hips toward the feet.

subtypes.name: Lotus and easy seats
subtypes.change: Tall seat for breathing. Cross-legged, lotus (feet on the thighs), butterfly (soles together), or kneeling on the heels (hero, thunderbolt: kneeFlex 160, no hip turn-out).

subtypes.name: Reclined and resting poses
subtypes.match: corpse|savasana|happy baby|pavanamuktasana|legs up the wall|reclining big toe
subtypes.change: Lying face up. Corpse: still and relaxed. Happy baby: knees to the armpits holding the feet. Legs up the wall: hips near the wall, legs vertical (hipFlex 90). Big toe pose: one straight leg raised with a strap.

subtypes.name: Mountain (standing)
subtypes.change: Stand tall, feet together or hip width, weight even, arms by the sides or overhead.

metrics.label: Head
metrics.good: in line with the spine; not loaded in inversions

motion.basis: Default keyframe is downward dog. Sun salutation hip, knee, ankle, elbow, wrist and spine angles from the 3-D motion capture of mullerpatan2019 (12 poses, timing from its pose durations); its knee in down dog (57°) and neck in cobra (-77°) were reduced to taught form, and shoulder flexion is estimated because that paper measured it differently. Standing-pose hip ranges checked against whissell2021 (triangle hip 90°) and the joint-moment profiles in wang2013, yu2012 and salem2013. All other pose angles are estimates from the classic shapes. Subtypes are listed most specific first; the first match wins. trunkRot (trunk rotation, + toward the right) is an extra key not yet in the README convention.
